title: At inovex's 500-person scale the fit is a reusable delivery asset, not a single integration
content:
inovex is around 500 people, runs roughly 90% of its projects on open source, and works in Kubernetes and edge/automotive. The open-source share matters as a screening signal: adopting an openly licensed component is normal there rather than exceptional, which removes a class of objection before it appears.

Size changes what fit means. At this scale a single client integration is not the interesting unit — it is one project among many and vanishes into the portfolio. The research states the alternative plainly: the fit is a reusable delivery asset that many engagements draw on, which is how a large consultancy turns a technology into revenue.

That framing has consequences for how the lead is worked. A reusable asset needs an internal owner and a standardisation decision, not just an interested engineer, so progress is measured in adoption inside the firm rather than in a first deployment. It is slower than the small-partner pattern elsewhere in the corpus, and more durable if it lands.
